When it comes to legal matters, it's essential to have access to a reliable and efficient court system. In Thurston County, Washington, the superior court plays a crucial role in handling civil and criminal cases. In this article, we'll explore everything you need to know about Thurston County Superior Court, from its history to its functions and services.

History of Thurston County Superior Court

Thurston County Superior Court was established in 1852, just four years after Washington became a state. The first superior court judge was John M. Murphy, who served from 1852 to 1855. Since then, the court has had 26 different judges, each contributing to the development of the court system in Thurston County.

Jurisdiction and Functions

Thurston County Superior Court is a trial court of general jurisdiction. It has the power to hear and decide on a wide range of cases, including civil, criminal, family, and juvenile matters. The court also has exclusive jurisdiction over some types of cases, such as divorce, adoption, and probate.

The superior court has two main divisions: the criminal division and the civil division. The criminal division handles criminal cases, including felonies and misdemeanors, while the civil division deals with civil cases, such as lawsuits, contract disputes, and property disputes.

Services Offered

Thurston County Superior Court offers a range of services to its clients, including:

Courtroom Proceedings

The court holds regular courtroom proceedings where cases are heard and decided upon. These proceedings are open to the public, except in cases where the judge orders otherwise. Court proceedings can be attended in person or viewed online through the court's website.

Jury Services

The court provides jury services to eligible citizens who are called upon to serve as jurors. Jurors play a vital role in the court system, as they help to ensure that trials are fair and impartial.

Alternative Dispute Resolution

Thurston County Superior Court offers alternative dispute resolution services, such as mediation and arbitration, to help parties resolve their disputes outside of the courtroom. These services are voluntary and confidential, and they can be an effective way to reach a resolution without going to trial.

Records Management

The court maintains records of all cases heard in its jurisdiction. These records are available to the public and can be accessed through the court's website or in person at the courthouse.
